### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/runtime`, touching **17** documentable anchor(s).

**52** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0c7869c03c9c6ff3a38bd6b09206edeee0184769`.

⛔ **11** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** cross-cutting symbol(s) contributed no route anchor: `recordId (4 routes)`
- **2** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `objectName (symbol, 58 pages)`, `sys_user (literal, 55 pages)`
- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **35** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0c7869c03c9c6ff3a38bd6b09206edeee0184769` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `fb02f7a29115e6eda2dfc28e5305fedf395a9c37` — the merge of head `0916d339e426a32f029081870c5764bc546b81ce` into base `0c7869c03c9c6ff3a38bd6b09206edeee0184769`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin fb02f7a29115e6eda2dfc28e5305fedf395a9c37 && git checkout fb02f7a29115e6eda2dfc28e5305fedf395a9c37
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 0c7869c03c9c6ff3a38bd6b09206edeee0184769 0916d339e426a32f029081870c5764bc546b81ce && git checkout -B drift-repro 0c7869c03c9c6ff3a38bd6b09206edeee0184769 && git merge --no-ff 0916d339e426a32f029081870c5764bc546b81ce

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0c7869c03c9c6ff3a38bd6b09206edeee0184769
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 0c7869c03c9c6ff3a38bd6b09206edeee0184769` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 席位核对

**L1 first review · ACCEPT** · head `0916d339e426a32f029081870c5764bc546b81ce` · card #34458 · read 2026-11-17T00:20Z

### Checklist (read on GitHub at this head, not from the report)

- **Shape:** draft, base `main`, body opens `Fixes #34458`. Closing-keyword scan of the whole body: one hit, `#34458`; the `#34457` and `#34429` mentions carry no keyword. `Fixes` is right: the card's done-when (the un-walled CONTROL leg flips to the admin id) is the flipped describe.
- **File surface:** 4 files from `get_files`, all named in claim 6931025801: `packages/metadata-protocol/src/seed-loader.ts` (listed "only if the person-reference resolution must move there", and it did), `packages/runtime/src/app-plugin.ts`, the wall test, the changeset. The claim's `plugin-security` files are untouched. Merges `e2ab3fd2` and `0916d339` bring `main` in; the three-dot diff holds only these 4.
- **Serial constraint:** `seed-loader.ts` is shared with open PR #34429; the body records `git merge-tree --write-tree` against `refs/pull/34429/head` exiting 0. Whichever of the two lands second re-reads that intersection on its landing head.
- **Changeset:** `.changeset/34458-unwalled-seed-person-refs.md`, `patch` on `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` and `@objectstack/runtime`, both published (no `private`); `@objectstack/organizations` is touched by a test only. Sentences checked against the diff: "holds each person reference its second pass left NULL, together with the row it landed on" (the push guarded by `stillUnresolved && deferred.targetObject === SystemObjectName.USER && heldRowId`); "writes it to that row only while the column is still NULL" (`where: { id: held.recordId, [held.field]: null }`); "A row the seed did not write keeps its value" (only held row ids are ever written); "A reference that still names nobody stays held until the next user insert of the process" (`stillHeld`, and the middleware fires on `sys_user` `create` / `insert` only); "The walled boot is unchanged" (the loader is kept only on the inline boot seed path).
- **Mechanism read:** retries are serialized through `heldPersonRetry`; the held list resets per `load`; the middleware runs after `next()`, returns at once when no loader is held, and releases the loader when `held === 0`; a failed retry is caught and logged at `warn`, so the user insert stands. A failed back-fill write is kept held and logged at `error` with the row, field and cause.
- **Tests:** the CONTROL describe flipped as the card requires (`assignee`, `reviewer`, `owner_id` all equal the admin id). The new describe has a PREMISE leg (NULL before the named person signs up, not filled by the admin's insert) and three outcome rows. The hand-assigned row keeping `adminId` pins the `[field]: null` compare-and-set; the guest row staying NULL pins ADR-0138 D1. No refusal path is added, so no `code`/`status` assertion is owed.
- **Positive control:** ablation of the handoff's loader read, proved in `packages/runtime/dist` by `ablation-dist-preflight.mjs` (the organizations suite imports built runtime), turns exactly the two new or flipped legs red (`2 failed | 3 passed`); restore leg proves the marker absent and 5/5 green.
- **Gates at this head:** check-runs on `0916d339…`: 51 runs, 35 `success`, 16 `skipped`, 0 failed; `Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check` and `Dogfood Regression Gate` `success`. Derived-gate round 72/72 (`--ran`: 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN).
- **Accepted deviation:** the derived-gate sweep spans two heads (`e2ab3fd2` for 67 families, `0916d339` for the rest) after a container restart; the merge between them touches none of the 4 files, and CI on the final head is the record.

### Out of scope, for the area to place (one line each: `filed #N` or `dropped — reason`)

- Acceptance note 1: the held references live in process memory, so a restart between the boot seed and the first admin's sign-up loses them. Not measured; a durable retry is a spec change (seed-settlement contract).
- Acceptance note 3: the pass-2 `UNRESOLVED` log still reads "No further seed pass retries this" while a held retry now follows for `sys_user` targets. Literally true, but an operator reading it may conclude the NULL is final.

### Body, no push

- The body has no attribution header; the project's two lines (the `claude-projects-attribution` comment and the "Requested by" line) open every PR body. A body edit.

### Owed after this

- **L2:** not owed. `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, no `(narrowing)`, no `packages/spec/src/**`, no governed path.
- **Landing tier:** `node scripts/pm/check-governed-merges.mjs --pr 34516`: 0 of 4 paths governed, 306 changed lines (+297 / −9) ≤ 3000 ⇒ ordinary queue landing by the area, on this head.
